text:
alex park: Anyone else hitting weird TS errors when using the JS SDK in the edge runtime? Generics + overloads explode once we ESM-build the sample app. Also noticed auth/retry behaves slightly different in edge vs node samples — could be our polyfills or fetch wrapper.

maria chen: yep saw that yesterday. can you paste a minimal repro?

alex park: here's the gist that fails after bundling:
```ts
// sdk client snippet
export function call<T>(opts: { input: T }): Promise<{ out: T }>;
export function call(opts: { input: unknown }): Promise<{ out: unknown }>;
export async function call(opts: any) { return { out: opts.input }; }

// usage in app.tsx
const res = await sdk.call({ input: { foo: 1 } });
res.out.foo // TS: Property 'foo' does not exist on type 'unknown'
```

locally (ts-node) it types fine, after bundling to ESM for edge it widens to unknown.

samir patel: I hit similar. bundlers + TS moduleResolution affect overload resolution. For edge builds we recommend `moduleResolution: 'bundler'` or `node16` depending on toolchain. A few notes: skipLibCheck hides these but that's not a fix. Also check `ts` emit and `declaration` settings — mixed ESM/CJS consumers can pick the wrong .d.ts.

maria chen: also the SDK exports shape matters. If package.json has only a single "main" field and bundler does odd path remapping, TS can lose inference. For our sample apps I think we accidentally shipped a patched .d.ts that turned a generic into unknown.

dev-bot: CI: sample-app-edge/ci #42 failed — typescript error in browser-bundle (tests: build-edge)

jordan lee: On the auth/retry parity: edge uses fetch + ephemeral token flow; node uses http agent + long-lived token cache. Edge retries currently avoid re-fetching auth token which can cause 401 -> no retry. We should unify behaviour or at least document the difference.

olivia ng: Proposed action items:
- update sample-app tsconfig to explicit `moduleResolution` for edge toolchain and include `types` minimal set.
- add a small test that builds the sample as ESM and runs `tsc --noEmit` in CI.
- add note in SDK README about unknown vs any behavior and a recommended pattern for callers (explicit generic param or as const where helpful).

maria chen: For overloads I'd prefer we simplify SDK typings: single generic with conditional types instead of multiple overloads that TS resolves differently across targets. It's less ergonomic but more stable.

alex park: That would help. Also can we add a tiny helper `sdk.callTyped<T>()` to force inference when callers opt in? That way we don't break existing ergonomic call sites.

samir patel: yup `callTyped<T>` is a good compromise. I'll sketch a PR that:
- changes overloads -> single generic + `callTyped` alias
- updates sample-app tsconfig for edge `moduleResolution: 'node16'` (we use esbuild + @vercel build)
- adds CI step `pnpm -w build --filter sample-app-edge && pnpm workspace sample-app-edge tsc --noEmit`

olivia ng: I'll file the sample-app PR and assign samir for the SDK typings PR. also adding a short doc blurb about auth/retry differences so onboarding isn't confusing.

alex park: amazing — thanks. can we also add a tiny note in the quickstart that if users see 'Property X does not exist on type unknown' they should try `as const` or callTyped<T> until we roll stability changes? saves a bunch of support noise.

maria chen: fine by me. one more FYI: bumping `skipLibCheck` in samples to true masks other issues; prefer explicit fixes.

olivia ng: Created GH issues: #2383 (sdk-typing-overloads->generic+callTyped), #2384 (sample-app-edge-tsconfig-and-ci), #2385 (edge-auth-retry-doc). I'll link PRs once ready. :white_check_mark:

samir patel: I'll start the typings PR this afternoon.

alex park: thanks all. tagging @devops for CI capacity if the new tsc step slows builds.

dev-bot: @devops requested — added a short CI alert to #eng-infra

jordan lee: once these land let's add a small blurb in release notes so customers expecting parity aren't surprised.

alex park: agreed. that'll reduce onboarding friction.

olivia ng: closing thread when PRs are open. thanks! :raised_hands:
